comment: The revert-check of `documentation-ownership`'s derived-reading-set requirements: one mutation per refusal — a glob that matches no tracked path, a named rule no glob reaches, and the `--diff` check that a change names every section the map derives for its paths. Run it with `bash tools/mutate.sh --mutations tools/check-rule-routes-mutations.json`; `.pi/skills/mutation-runner` owns how, `.pi/skills/revert-check` owns the rule, and the CI step that owns the rule routes prints `--list`, so a set that no longer parses fails the pipeline instead of rotting. `case-cmd` runs one named case (`--case {case}`), so a mutation pays one case and not the suite. The search is a single line and unique in its file, because the runner's replacement is literal and line-based, and the file is restored byte for byte afterwards.

mutations.label: glob-matches-the-tree
mutations.why: every glob is matched against the tree's tracked paths, so a glob that matches nothing is reported instead of silently orphaning the rules a reader is told to read

mutations.label: rule-is-reached
mutations.why: every named rule under guidelines/ is compared with the rules the map reaches, so a rule no glob reaches is reported before it has a violation

mutations.label: change-names-the-derived-set
mutations.why: a change may add a section to its derived reading set and never shrink it, so a derived section the change's artifacts do not name is reported
